ai-hpc.h3: Meta launches Muse, a personal agent that can email, book and pay
ai-hpc.summary: Meta released Muse to US users on Tuesday 8 September, a personal AI agent powered by its Muse Spark model that can send emails, book travel, fill out forms and make purchases on a user's behalf.
body: Meta on Tuesday 8 September launched Muse, a personal AI agent for adults in the United States, available on the web at muse.ai, through iOS and Android apps and inside WhatsApp chats. According to TechCrunch and Bloomberg, users share a goal and the agent builds a plan, opens a browser, fills in forms and completes tasks such as booking trips, sending party invitations, lowering bills and buying goods through Link by Stripe. The service is free at launch with paid Power and Maximum tiers at $20 and $100 a month.

Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang told reporters the agent runs in an isolated environment inside Meta's infrastructure and never sees a user's passwords or payment details. The launch is a direct test of whether consumers will hand Meta access to email, calendars, payments and health services, TechCrunch noted, given the company's history of privacy controversies.

ai-hpc.h3: Mistral raises EUR 3bn at EUR 21bn valuation in Samsung-led round
ai-hpc.summary: Paris-based Mistral AI closed a EUR 3 billion Series D on Tuesday 8 September, the largest equity round ever for a European tech company, with Samsung Electronics leading.
body: Samsung led the round alongside EQT's Scaleup Europe Fund and existing investor PSG Equity, according to TechCrunch and Euronews. New backers include Advent, BlackRock funds and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, while a16z, ASML, General Catalyst, Lightspeed, Nvidia and Salesforce Ventures returned. The post-money valuation tops EUR 21 billion, close to double the EUR 11.7 billion Series C a year earlier.

CEO Arthur Mensch told CNBC the money goes mainly into owning data centers and renting additional compute, which ties the raise to the same sovereign AI infrastructure push that saw Google's Marc Oman join Mistral Compute this week.

ai-hpc.h3: IREN's 2GW Sweetwater hub wins conditional ERCOT base load status
ai-hpc.summary: IREN said on Tuesday 8 September that its 1,400MW Sweetwater 1 and 600MW Sweetwater 2 projects in Texas were conditionally classified as base load under ERCOT's Batch Zero process.
body: IREN announced on 8 September that its 2GW Sweetwater data center hub in West Texas received conditional base load classification under ERCOT's Batch Zero interconnection framework, TheEnergyMag reported. The designation covers both Sweetwater 1 at 1,400MW and Sweetwater 2 at 600MW and places the projects in the grid operator's planning baseline rather than requiring further study. IREN stressed the classification remains subject to ongoing approvals.

The Sweetwater 1 high-voltage substation was energized earlier this year and construction of 300MW of gross data center capacity continues with delivery targeted for the fourth quarter of 2027. IREN also said additional large pipeline projects were included in Batch Zero but did not disclose their locations or sizes.

ai-hpc.h3: Soluna completes 83MW Kati 1, whole 166MW campus cleared by ERCOT
ai-hpc.summary: Soluna Holdings said on Tuesday 8 September it energized the final 14MW at Project Kati 1 in Texas, lifting company capacity to about 206MW, while ERCOT conditionally classified the full 166MW Kati campus as base load.
body: Soluna Holdings announced on 8 September that it had completed its 83MW Kati 1 bitcoin hosting facility in Willacy County, Texas, after energizing the final 14MW tranche, TheEnergyMag reported. Companywide operating capacity rose to roughly 206MW. The wind-powered site hosts a 28MW co-mining arrangement with Bitdeer that starts deployment this month.

The company also said ERCOT conditionally classified the entire 166MW Kati campus, including its planned AI expansion, as base load under the Batch Zero process. According to Soluna the designation preserves interconnection capacity based on earlier studies and exempts the campus from further reliability evaluation or megawatt allocation within the batch.

ai-hpc.h3: TSMC and Samsung commit to ASML's $400m High NA EUV tools
ai-hpc.summary: TSMC and Samsung said on Tuesday 8 September they will adopt ASML's High NA EUV lithography machines, citing the complex transistor architectures demanded by AI chips.
body: ASML secured commitments from both TSMC and Samsung for its High NA EUV lithography systems, CNBC and the Taipei Times reported on 8 and 9 September. Samsung plans to use the tools for DRAM production from 2028 while TSMC expects adoption for advanced logic around 2030. The machines cost about $400 million each and print finer circuit patterns than current EUV systems.

TSMC said its use of High NA machines would rise over time, driven primarily by the increasingly complex transistor architectures required for AI applications. Intel was the first customer to install the tools and the decisions by its two largest rivals broaden the customer base for ASML's most expensive product line.

ai-hpc.h3: Qualcomm and AWS team up on custom inference silicon and 1.6T optics
ai-hpc.summary: Qualcomm and Amazon announced a multi-generational partnership on Tuesday 8 September to co-develop custom AI inference chips and optical connectivity up to 1.6T for AWS data centers.
body: Qualcomm Technologies and Amazon Web Services announced on 8 September a multi-generational agreement to develop customized silicon for large-scale AI data centers, with a focus on inference, Data Center Dynamics reported. The two companies will also build optical connectivity solutions scaling to 1.6T using Qualcomm's SerDes and optical DSP technology.

AWS already designs its own Trainium and Inferentia accelerators and Graviton CPUs, and the deal adds Qualcomm's low-power processing expertise to that roadmap. Qualcomm in turn will expand its own use of AWS infrastructure, including Amazon Bedrock, for chip design automation workloads.

ai-hpc.h3: Palantir picks Nebius as preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner
ai-hpc.summary: Palantir named neocloud Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure provider on Tuesday 8 September, bringing Nebius compute and inference endpoints inside Palantir's enterprise security perimeter.
body: Palantir Technologies and Nebius Group announced on 8 September that Nebius will be Palantir's preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner, Data Center Dynamics reported. Eligible Palantir commercial customers gain access to Nebius cloud and inference capacity and can deploy and adapt open models on Nebius hardware using their own data, with Palantir's AIP, Ontology, Foundry and Apollo stack providing the authorization and isolation layer.

Nebius said in its newsroom post that the companies plan to jointly accelerate new AI compute capacity, including modular data center deployments at sites where power is already available. Nebius shares rose in pre-market trading after the announcement.

ai-hpc.h3: OpenAI anchors two Firmus AI data centers in Malaysia as Korea stalls
ai-hpc.summary: Firmus signed a multi-year capacity deal with OpenAI for two Malaysian AI data centers on Tuesday 8 September, while OpenAI's Stargate project in South Korea is reportedly stuck at the starting gate.
body: Firmus announced on 8 September a multi-year agreement under which OpenAI will be the anchor customer at two of its AI data centers in Malaysia, Data Center Dynamics reported. The deal lifts Firmus' total contracted capacity across all customers above 900MW. The company operates or is developing seven AI data centers across Australia, Singapore, Indonesia and Malaysia, five of which are due within 24 months using Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 systems in its prefabricated HyperCube modules.

OpenAI compute strategy VP Sachin Katti said the Malaysian sites would help serve growing regional demand. Firmus co-CEO Tim Rosenfield called it the moment Asia-Pacific becomes a producer of intelligence rather than just a consumer.

ai-hpc.h3: Anthropic has signed $517bn of compute deals in 11 months, report says
ai-hpc.summary: An analysis by The Information published Monday 7 September puts Anthropic's compute commitments since October 2025 at up to $517 billion covering 14.8GW, with Google and AWS supplying 11GW of that.
body: Anthropic has signed agreements covering roughly 14.8GW of compute capacity since October 2025, with a combined maximum value of about $517 billion, according to an analysis by The Information that Data Center Dynamics summarized on 7 September. Google and AWS together account for around 11GW, with the remainder spread across Microsoft, Nscale, SpaceX's xAI data centers and other providers.

The figure is an upper-bound estimate compiled from cloud commitments, chip capacity and long-term data center leases, many of which phase in over several years and may not be used at their maximum contracted level. It compares with an earlier internal projection of about $180 billion in server rental spending through 2029.

ai-hpc.h3: Nevada regulators weigh Fleet's private gas plants for Reno data centers
ai-hpc.summary: The Public Utility Commission of Nevada took up Fleet Data Centers' request on Tuesday 8 September to build two methane-fired plants totaling more than 360MW for its Tahoe Reno Industrial Center campuses.
body: Fleet Data Centers, a Tract Capital subsidiary, is seeking approval from the Public Utility Commission of Nevada to build two gas-fired power plants to serve its Peru Ridge and South Valley campuses at the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Data Center Dynamics reported on 8 September. The plants would generate more than 360MW using methane-fired engines and a decision was expected within days.

Nevada Current reported the facilities would burn about three times as much gas as NV Energy's entire Northern Nevada residential and commercial customer base used in 2025. Opponents argue that private generation for data centers sidesteps the state's renewable portfolio standard, which requires providers to reach 50 percent renewables by 2030.

ai-hpc.h3: Google's European energy chief jumps to Mistral Compute for 1GW push
ai-hpc.summary: Marc Oman, who led energy sourcing for Google's European data centers for nearly 12 years, joined Mistral Compute on Tuesday 8 September as the lab targets more than 1GW of European capacity by 2030.
body: Marc Oman, head of energy sourcing strategy for Google's data centers and colocation sites across Europe, has left for Mistral Compute, Data Center Dynamics reported on 8 September. Mistral Compute is the newly formed division that provides private HPC resources for training and running the company's models. Oman will be based at Mistral's new Paris headquarters.

In a LinkedIn post Oman said he personally led the closing of more than 2GW of solar and wind power purchase agreements for Google across nine European countries including the Netherlands. He framed the move as a bet on European technological sovereignty and reducing dependence on foreign hyperscalers.

ai-hpc.h3: MiniMax Sol-H3 renders 5 seconds of video in 1.65 seconds on B300
ai-hpc.summary: MiniMax and Nvidia Research released Sol-H3 on Monday 7 September, an inference stack that generates five seconds of 1344x768 video with stereo audio in 1.653 seconds on an 8-GPU Nvidia B300 system.
body: MiniMax released Sol-H3, its fastest end-to-end inference stack for the MiniMax-H3 video model, with details published on Nvidia Research's Sol Engine page and announced by researcher Enze Xie on 7 September. On a single 8x Nvidia B300 Blackwell system the stack produces five seconds of 1344x768 video with stereo audio in 1.653 seconds, faster than real-time playback.

The engineering combines dynamic sparse attention without retraining, fused norm and MLP kernels, INT8 QKV and FP8 output communication across the eight GPUs, parallel batched VAE decoding and cached AdaLN computation. Across 1x, 4x and 8x B300 configurations the team reports up to a 15.54x speedup over the base H3 pipeline.

ai-hpc.h3: ChatGPT Work now learns your writing style from Gmail and Slack
ai-hpc.summary: OpenAI rolled out a Writing style setting for ChatGPT Work around Monday 7 September that studies connected Gmail, Google Drive, Slack and SharePoint content to mimic a user's phrasing and sign-offs.
body: OpenAI has added a personalization option to ChatGPT Work that lets the assistant reflect a user's own writing style in new drafts, AlternativeTo and BusinessToday reported on 7 and 8 September. Users connect Gmail, Google Drive, Slack or SharePoint and enable the option under Settings, Personalization and Writing style.

The system analyzes emails, messages and files from those connectors to pick up recurring phrases, sentence structure, capitalization habits and how a person signs off. It does not learn from what users type directly into ChatGPT, only from the connected workplace sources.

ai-hpc.h3: Gemini quietly adds Immersive View to its Students tab
ai-hpc.summary: Google's Gemini app has surfaced an Immersive View feature in its Students section, spotted on Monday 7 September, which turns topics such as dinosaurs and quasars into zoomable image-based mind maps.
body: TestingCatalog reported on 7 September that Gemini's Students tab now offers Immersive View, a browsing mode in which users pick a topic such as the dinosaur era or space quasars and receive an image annotated with clickable nodes. Each node opens a deeper page with its own nodes, building an image-based mind map that can descend five or more levels, in some cases down to atoms and molecules.

It is unclear whether the feature is still in testing or has begun a wider rollout. Google has been expanding Gemini's education footprint, including bringing Gemini in Classroom to students of all ages in August.

ai-hpc.h3: China targets 9,800 exaflops of AI compute by 2030, four times today
ai-hpc.summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology published a 2026-2030 plan on Monday 7 September that aims to lift national intelligent computing capacity to 9,800 exaflops and calls for 3.8 trillion yuan of infrastructure spending.
body: MIIT's 15th Five-Year Plan for the information and communications industry, posted publicly on 7 September, sets a 2030 target of 9,800 exaflops of intelligent computing power, the South China Morning Post reported. That is more than four times the roughly 2,185 exaflops recorded in June 2026 and compares with 1,590 exaflops for 2025.

The plan pairs the compute goal with a storage target of 1,700 exabytes by 2030, up from 540 exabytes, and calls for 3.8 trillion yuan, about $532 billion, of cumulative information infrastructure investment over the period. It endorses the orderly deployment of clusters with 10,000 and 100,000 or more GPU cards plus inference facilities tailored to specific applications.

ai-hpc.h3: Alibaba Cloud and Cambricon take Platinum seats at PyTorch Foundation
ai-hpc.summary: The PyTorch Foundation announced on Tuesday 8 September at its Shanghai conference that Alibaba Cloud and Cambricon joined as Platinum members with board seats, while Ant Group joined at Gold level.
body: The PyTorch Foundation said on 8 September at PyTorch Conference China 2026 in Shanghai that Alibaba Cloud and chip designer Cambricon have joined as Platinum members, each receiving a seat on the Governing Board and the Technical Advisory Council. Ant Group joined as a Gold member. The three new members delivered keynotes alongside existing member Huawei.

Talks covered serving Alibaba's Qwen models at scale, device-agnostic PyTorch and Kubernetes-based agent runtimes. Cambricon maintains open source toolkits, drivers and ML pipelines for its MLU accelerator hardware, and its membership deepens PyTorch support for Chinese domestic silicon.

ai-hpc.h3: China's AI data center boom shifts to the north and northwest
ai-hpc.summary: Bloomberg reported on Tuesday 8 September that more than half of China's data center pipeline now sits in northern and northwestern regions such as Inner Mongolia, sidestepping the land and power constraints seen in the US and Europe.
body: China is relocating AI computing capacity away from its crowded eastern megacities toward western and northern regions with cheap power, cool climates and open land, Bloomberg reported on 8 September. BloombergNEF data show more than half of the country's data center pipeline is already in the north and northwest, and those regions are expected to overtake the major cities in total capacity by 2028.

The shift follows the state-directed Eastern Data, Western Computing initiative launched in 2021 and 2022. Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia, a city of under two million people, has become a front line for the buildout. China's total data center electricity use is projected to nearly double to 329 terawatt-hours by 2030.

ai-hpc.h3: Baidu's Xiaodu puts an upgraded AI agent into home cameras and screens
ai-hpc.summary: Baidu's smart device unit Xiaodu unveiled new displays, companion screens, speakers and cameras on Tuesday 8 September, all running an upgraded Super Xiaodu assistant with a second-generation monitoring agent.
body: Xiaodu, Baidu's smart hardware business, held a launch event in Beijing on 8 September introducing a lineup of smart displays, Tiantian companion screens, speakers and cameras built around the upgraded Super Xiaodu AI assistant, TechNode reported. The assistant is being repositioned from voice helper to household agent.

The cameras carry a second-generation AI monitoring agent that interprets scenes, detects anomalies and responds without user prompts, according to tech-ish, marking a shift toward proactive home security rather than passive recording.

ai-hpc.h3: Xpeng switches on automated line for its IRON humanoid robot
ai-hpc.summary: Xpeng activated what it calls the world's first automated production line for advanced humanoid robots on Monday 7 September, with the first IRON unit walking off the line and mass production targeted for year-end.
body: Xpeng announced on 7 September that it had activated an automated production line for its IRON humanoid robot, with the first unit completing assembly and walking off the line on its own, TechNode and Electrek reported. The company says core processes are more than 80 percent automated and the line borrows automotive-grade quality systems from its EV plants.

IRON has 76 degrees of freedom and runs three in-house Turing AI chips delivering up to 2,250 TOPS alongside a second-generation vision-language-action foundation model. Xpeng plans volume production by the end of 2026 with initial deployments in its own stores and campuses, followed by deliveries in China and overseas in 2027.

ai-hpc.h3: Cognition raises $2bn at $48bn as Devin revenue nears $900m
ai-hpc.summary: Cognition, maker of the Devin coding agent, announced a $2 billion Series E on Tuesday 8 September at a $48 billion valuation, nearly double the $26 billion mark it set just four months ago.
body: Cognition said on 8 September it had raised $2 billion at a $48 billion valuation in a round led by Andreessen Horowitz, Accel, Founders Fund, General Catalyst and Avenir, TechCrunch and Bloomberg reported. Benchmark, Bessemer, Kleiner Perkins, Greylock, Lightspeed and Nvidia also participated.

Annualized run-rate revenue has grown from $492 million in May to almost $900 million, according to Bloomberg. The previous round in May valued the company at $26 billion, so the valuation has nearly doubled in four months.

ai-hpc.h3: OpenHands hits 1.0 with sandboxing and 68% on SWE-bench Verified
ai-hpc.summary: The open source coding agent OpenHands shipped its 1.0 release this week with production Docker sandboxing, built-in security policies, resource limits and a plugin system.
body: OpenHands, the open source autonomous coding agent formerly known as OpenDevin, reached version 1.0 with production-ready Docker sandboxing, security policies, resource limits and a plugin system, according to the project's GitHub releases page and a DEV Community write-up published this week. The team reports the agent completes about 68 percent of SWE-bench Verified tasks autonomously.

The SDK ships a ConfirmRisky policy paired with an LLM-based security analyzer that pauses the agent on high-risk tool calls such as destructive shell commands or anything touching credentials until a human approves.

ai-hpc.h3: GitHub Copilot app lets developers run several agents in parallel
ai-hpc.summary: GitHub's Copilot app now runs multiple specialized agents at once, each in its own isolated git worktree, so implementation, testing and documentation can proceed on the same repository without conflicts.
body: GitHub has expanded its Copilot app so developers can launch and supervise several agent sessions in parallel, GitHub's blog and AlphaSignal reported in the first week of September. Each session runs in its own git worktree, so multiple agents can work on the same repository simultaneously without overwriting one another's changes.

A developer can, for example, ask one agent to build a feature, another to run an accessibility review and a third to execute the test suite, then track all three through a unified session view. GitHub pitches the app as a control center for orchestrating agents rather than a single assistant.

ai-hpc.h3: Accenture and Google Cloud form 1,000-engineer Gemini deployment unit
ai-hpc.summary: Google Cloud and Accenture launched the Accenture Gemini Enterprise Business Group on Tuesday 8 September, a joint unit of 1,000 forward-deployed engineers to embed Google's AI in large enterprises.
body: Accenture and Google Cloud announced on 8 September a dedicated business group that will send forward-deployed engineers into enterprises to implement Gemini Enterprise and Google's agentic AI tools, TechCrunch and HPCwire reported. The unit is being staffed with a 1,000-person engineering workforce.

TechCrunch framed the move as Google racing to catch up in the AI deployment wars. OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Amazon have all recently created their own forward-deployed engineering units on the bet that implementing models inside customers can become a trillion-dollar business in its own right.

ai-hpc.h3: OECD: students who use AI chatbots daily score 28 points lower in science
ai-hpc.summary: The OECD's PISA 2025 report released Tuesday 8 September found that students who never use AI to draft schoolwork scored 509 in science against 481 for daily users, a gap of roughly a year and a half of teaching.
body: The OECD published its PISA 2025 results on 8 September covering more than 760,000 students in 91 countries, Bloomberg reported. Students who never or almost never use AI to draft texts for writing assignments scored 509 on the science test compared with 481 for those who do so every day, a 28-point gap the OECD equates to about a year and a half of schooling.

Similar patterns appeared for using AI to do preliminary research or summarize assigned reading. The one exception was students who used AI weekly specifically to help them learn, who scored highest at around 500 points. Daily users scored 13 points higher when teachers consistently asked them to critique AI-produced content.

ai-hpc.h3: SAP's own board wants an AI breakthrough within months, Bloomberg reports
ai-hpc.summary: Bloomberg reported on Tuesday 8 September that SAP supervisory board members believe the German software giant needs a genuine AI breakthrough in the coming months after its shares fell roughly 47 percent over the past year.
body: Members of SAP's supervisory board think the company must deliver an AI breakthrough in the coming months or fall painfully behind rivals, Bloomberg reported in a feature published on 8 September. Some directors see two years as the outer limit while others believe one is more realistic. SAP shares have lost about 47 percent over the past year as AI has rattled the enterprise software sector.

The company has frozen hiring and travel, reshuffled leadership so the CEO and COO directly oversee AI products, and committed more than EUR 1 billion to a new AI lab built around its Prior Labs acquisition.
